# Feature: Plain-Field Fill Performance & Batch Clarity

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-057
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_do_workflow_reliability.md` (§5 G6 and "Measured"; §6 "Tools" row `browser_fill_form`, `browser_fill_element`; §8 "Sequencing"; §9 "Advice may only name an engineered move", "A tool result says what happened"; §10 "Counted, not timed"; §11 FEAT-057; §12 FEAT-057; §13 rows 7 and 10)

An ordinary text box should cost well under a second to fill and verify. In run `20261014T023539Z-do-7039cbaa`, each plain text fill took about five seconds, and the first ten-field batch took 56.45 s. A form with 40 or more controls cannot finish in a reasonable time at that rate. The model is also never told how many fields one call accepts or how many remain after a batch.

**The mechanism (verified against current source).**

1. **Every text fill waits the full four seconds.** `buildTextPlan` enters its `watch-and-select` rung whenever text was entered ([`plans.ts:186-196`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/plans.ts#L186-L196)). That rung calls `watchAndSelectOffered`, which polls `readReaction` through `readWhenStable` with `accept: reaction.ignored || reaction.candidates.length > 0` ([`combobox-driver.ts:409-425`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts#L409-L425)). A plain input never produces candidates, so `accept` is never true and the loop runs until `REACTION_WAIT_MS = 4_000` expires ([`combobox-driver.ts:60`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts#L60)). The wait is right for a late autocomplete and pure waste for a plain box.
2. **Declared suggestion controls never reach that rung.** A control with `role="combobox"`, a list-type `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, or `aria-controls` pointing at a list scores above zero in `scoreComboboxShape` ([`combobox-driver.ts:84-121`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts#L84-L121)). The engine then drives it through the combobox family before the text plan is built ([`engine.ts:228-246`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L228-L246)). The text plan's four-second watch therefore runs almost entirely on controls that declared nothing. Every existing late-suggestion gauntlet fixture declares `aria-autocomplete="list"`, so none of them exercises that watch.
3. **On a default install, a ten-field batch times out.** The default per-tool timeout is 45 s (`DEFAULT_BUDGET_LIMITS.perToolTimeoutMs`, [`budget.ts:109`](../../../packages/agent/src/runtime/budget.ts#L109)). The historical run finished its 56.45 s batch only because that user's `profile.yaml` sets `tool_timeout: 3m`. Plan §12 cites a 180-second timeout. That is the user's override, not the default. On a fresh install, today's ten plain fields take about 50 s and exceed the limit.
4. **Every applied entry carries its full recovery ledger.** The engine attaches `attempted` whenever more than one non-skipped verdict exists ([`engine.ts:452`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L452)). An ordinary plain fill records the typing rung, `enter-text`, and `watch-and-select`, so every applied field carries a ledger the model has no use for ([`browser-fill-element.ts:269`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts#L269), [`browser-fill-form.ts:196`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L196)).
5. **The cap is unstated, and the example is task-shaped.** `maxItems: 10` exists only in the schema ([`browser-fill-form.ts:47`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L47)). An eleven-field call fails with the generic `Invalid tool input at "/fields": …`. The `do` addendum teaches batching with a travel search: "one call for the whole search form (destination, dates, travellers)" ([`profiles.ts:122-128`](../../../packages/agent/src/runtime/profiles.ts#L122-L128)).

This feature delivers five things:

1. **A tighter `watch-and-select` entry, written as plan data.** The text plan gains a short `reaction-check` rung. The full watch runs only when the control declares suggestion behavior in closed state, or the short rung observed a popup. Every other input pays one bounded reaction window (`REACTION_PROBE_MS`) plus normal verification. The four-second settling policy, late-suggestion coverage, and the no-Enter rule are unchanged.
2. **A stated cap with a cause-specific overflow message.** One constant, `FILL_FORM_MAX_FIELDS = 10`, feeds the schema, the tool description, and the `do` addendum. An over-cap call returns `INVALID_INPUT / batch-limit`, which names the limit, the count sent, and the next move: send the first ten, then the rest.
3. **Shape-neutral guidance.** The travel example is replaced. The addendum and both fill-tool descriptions teach bounded batches in page order and how to continue.
4. **Compact results, with the ledger in the audit.** An applied field that landed exactly with no recovery is reported as `{ field, ref, resolution: "exact" }`, plus `committed` only when its text differs. Every other field keeps full detail. The full entries, ledgers included, go to `details.applied`, which `tool-calls.jsonl` records.
5. **Progress and remaining counts in every fill result.** `progress: { filled, eligible, remaining, next }` reports what this run has verified on this document and lists up to ten unfilled eligible controls by ref and label. It is computed from the observation the tool already takes, with no extra page read, using the same coverage function as FEAT-054's `fill` evaluation.

**Acceptance** (plan §12 FEAT-057, §13 row 7):

- **No wasted wait.** A static plain input does not pay the four-second suggestion wait, asserted by counting reaction reads.
- **Tool-time target.** 40 controls are filled and verified within 60 s of browser/tool time on a controlled local fixture.
- **Default timeout.** Each ten-field plain batch finishes in at most 15 s of tool time, well inside the 45 s default per-tool timeout. This is a check added by this spec (see deviation 1).
- **No regressions.** Late suggestions, masked inputs, and date-range groups remain correct. An undeclared control that shows a popup inside the probe window still gets the full watch.
- **No resends.** A committed field is not resent because another field failed, either inside a batch or by following `progress.next`.
- **User-side target ⚠ (observational).** End-to-end p50 ≤ 2 min and p95 ≤ 5 min on a fixture larger than the cap, with capture, is measured by FEAT-060's live benchmark. It does not gate this feature.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope: G6 in full, and plan §12 FEAT-057 scope and acceptance.

Out of scope:

- **A larger-batch interface.** Raising `maxItems` to 40 is explicitly rejected by plan §12. An engine-partitioned batch that honors a shared deadline, preserves widget groups, and accounts for every applied, failed, and unattempted field is recorded in TODO.
- **Field identity, labels, the census, and continuation** (FEAT-055). This feature reads FEAT-055's census and registry. It does not change them.
- **Coverage evaluation and the action ledger** (FEAT-054). This feature reuses FEAT-054's coverage computation for its progress counts. It does not change how `fill` is judged.
- **Protected-value readback** (FEAT-056). The new rung reads the committed value through whichever read the text plan uses when this lands. FEAT-056 makes that read honest. This feature changes only when the full watch runs.
- **Progress events on stderr and `--json`** (FEAT-059). FEAT-059 emits `progress: fields 20/48` from the same coverage function. This feature puts the counts in the tool result only.
- **Combobox-driver timing.** Declared suggestion controls keep their full choreography and wait.
- **The settled-stale-list problem** (TODO line 273). Unchanged.

### Deviations and clarifications (flagged, awaiting confirmation)

1. **CLARIFICATION: the per-tool timeout is 45 s by default, not 180 s.** Plan §12 reasons that "a 40-field batch can exceed the 180-second tool timeout". 180 s is the historical user's `tool_timeout: 3m`. The default is 45 s, so today's ten-field batch already exceeds a fresh install's limit. This spec adds a gate: a ten-field plain batch takes ≤ 15 s of tool time (a quarter of the 60 s target for 40). The plan's conclusion, keeping the cap at ten, is unchanged and gets stronger.
2. **DEVIATION: a `list` attribute pointing at a native `<datalist>` does not trigger the full watch.** Plan §12 lists "a `list`/datalist" among the closed-state signals. Chrome draws native datalist suggestions in browser UI, outside the DOM. `readReaction` can never see them, so a four-second watch on a datalist input would always time out, which is the waste this feature removes. A native datalist accepts free text, so the typed value stands. If the page draws its own popup for that input, the `reaction-check` rung sees it and escalates. Selecting a datalist option by its offered label is recorded in TODO. **Awaiting confirmation.**
3. **CLARIFICATION: `aria-controls` and `aria-owns` alone do not declare suggestions.** The engine's `shape.linkedPopup` includes them, and they keep their current role in the editee probe and the ignored-container read ([`engine.ts:131-141`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L131-L141), [`engine.ts:262-267`](../../../packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts#L262-L267)). They are not in the plan's list. They often point at a status or error region, as `scoreComboboxShape`'s own comment notes, and one that does point at a real list is already claimed by the combobox driver.
4. **CLARIFICATION: what "declared" reaches the text plan.** Because the combobox family claims the strong declarations first (point 2 of the mechanism), the text plan's declared branch is reached in practice by the remaining declarations only: `aria-haspopup` values other than `listbox` and `false` (`true`, `menu`, `dialog`, `grid`, `tree`), or a combobox-family attempt that did not engage. The predicate still checks the plan's full list, so that the rule stays what the plan says and survives changes to combobox detection.
5. **CLARIFICATION: the probe window is calibrated, not guessed.** `REACTION_PROBE_MS` starts at 450 ms, which is four reads at the existing 150 ms poll. TASK-001 measures the baseline. TASK-002 keeps the value only if both conditions hold: an undeclared popup that renders 300 ms after the last keystroke is still caught, and the 40-control fixture stays within its target. A popup that first appears after the window on an undeclared control is missed. This is the accepted cost of the tighter entry, and it is recorded in TODO beside line 273.
6. **ADDITION: `progress.next`.** Plan §12 asks for "remaining counts, so another observation is unnecessary after each batch". Counts alone do not say which fields remain, and the model would need a continuation `browser_observe` to find them. `next` lists at most ten remaining eligible controls (one batch) by ref and label. The refs come from FEAT-055's registry, which `browser_fill_*` already accepts without re-observing, so the advice names an engineered move (memory → Coding Standards).
7. **CLARIFICATION: prompt version.** The addendum text changes, so `PROMPT_VERSION` moves to the next version: `agent-v12` if FEAT-054's `agent-v11` has landed, otherwise `agent-v11`, and FEAT-054 takes the version after it. FEAT-055 deviation 7 already assigns the batch wording to this feature.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No relational store, and `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature adds in-memory core and agent types, one model-visible result key, and one message-catalog entry. No persisted schema changes. `tool-calls.jsonl` already records `details`.

### Core: text plan (`fill/plans.ts`)

- **`BuildTextPlanInput`** gains:
  - `declaredSuggestions` (boolean): the closed-state signal from the engine's shape read.
  - `runReaction` (`(context) => Promise<RungOutcome<TValue, TFailure>>`): the short reaction check. It is injected, so plan tests can count it (memory: a module-internal call needs a real seam).
- **Rungs, in order:**

| Rung                   | Axis | Entry                                                                                                                 | Cost cap                         | Produces                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enter-text`           | how  | always (unchanged)                                                                                                    | `min(maxActions, 6)` (unchanged) | `text-entered`, `committed`, `editee`                     |
| `reaction-check` (new) | what | `text-entered === true` and `declaredSuggestions === false`; else unmet `suggestions-declared` or `control-not-empty` | 0 actions (reads only)           | `popup-observed`, `committed`                             |
| `watch-and-select`     | what | `text-entered === true` and (`declaredSuggestions` or `popup-observed === true`); else unmet `no-suggestion-signal`   | `min(maxActions, 2)` (unchanged) | `offered`, `chosen`, `committed`, `container` (unchanged) |

- **Entry evidence tokens:** `suggestions-declared` (declared branch), `popup-observed` (observed branch).
- The runner keeps the last successful outcome, so a plain input ends on `reaction-check`'s outcome when `watch-and-select` is skipped ([`escalation.ts:469-482`](../../../packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts#L469-L482)).

### Core: reaction probe (`widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts`)

- **`REACTION_PROBE_MS`** (exported const, starting value `450`): the longest an undeclared control is watched for a popup after typing. Calibrated by TASK-001 and TASK-002 (deviation 5).
- **`observeReaction(port, target, scope): Promise<ReactionProbe>`** (exported): polls `readReaction` every `REACTION_POLL_MS` until `REACTION_PROBE_MS` or the budget deadline, whichever is first. It returns as soon as a popup is observed. Otherwise it reads the committed value once at the end of the window.
- **`ReactionProbe`**: `{ popupObserved: true; container: WidgetContainer } | { popupObserved: false; committed: <the text plan's committed read> }`.
  - **Popup observed** means `!reaction.ignored && reaction.container !== null && reaction.open`. Zero candidates still counts: a popup that is still loading escalates to the full watch, which waits for content.
  - The committed read is `readCommitted` today, or FEAT-056's typed read once it lands. It is the same function `watchAndSelectOffered`'s `no-suggestions` branch uses.
- `REACTION_WAIT_MS`, `REACTION_QUIET_POLLS`, and `watchAndSelectOffered` are unchanged.

### Core: shape read (`fill/engine.ts`)

- **`shape.declaresSuggestions`** (boolean, computed in the existing single `evaluateOn` shape read; no added page read):
  - `role="combobox"`, or
  - `aria-autocomplete` in `list | both | inline`, or
  - `aria-haspopup` present and not `false`, or
  - `HTMLInputElement.list` resolves to an element that is **not** a native `HTMLDataListElement` (deviation 2).
- `shape.linkedPopup` keeps its current definition and uses (deviation 3).

### Agent: batch limit (`adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts`)

- **`FILL_FORM_MAX_FIELDS = 10`** (exported const): the schema's `maxItems`, the number interpolated into the tool description, and the number in the `do` addendum. A test pins that all three agree.

### Agent: invalid-input advice (`runtime/middleware.ts`, `runtime/messages.ts`)

- **`ToolWrapperSpec.inputAdvice?`**: `(raw: unknown) => { cause: string; details: Record<string, unknown> } | null`. The middleware consults it only after `Check` fails and before rendering the generic `INVALID_INPUT / schema-validation`. A null return keeps the generic message. The hook never makes invalid input valid.
- **Message catalog entry `INVALID_INPUT / batch-limit`**: tool scope, detail keys `sent` and `limit`, capability `browser_fill_form`. Rendered text:

  > `browser_fill_form takes at most 10 fields per call and this call sent 13. Send the first 10 now, then the remaining 3 in a following browser_fill_form call.`

### Agent: model-visible fill result

- **Compact applied entry** (`browser_fill_form` `applied[]`, and the top level of a `browser_fill_element` success). This is used when **all** of the following hold:
  - `resolution === 'exact'`;
  - no `editee`, `offered`, `note`, or `substitution`;
  - the ledger holds no `failed` verdict;
  - at most one typing strategy was performed.

  Shape: `{ field, ref, resolution: 'exact' }`, plus `committed` only when its text differs from `requested`, plus `covers` when present. FEAT-056's `withheld` key, when present, is always kept.

- **Full applied entry**: unchanged from today (`field`, `ref`, `driver`, `dismissed`, `actions`, `committed`, `requested`, `resolution`, `offered?`, `note?`, `attempted?`, `editee?`, `covers?`).
- **`details.applied`** (audit only, never model-visible): every applied entry in full form, `attempted` included, in caller order. Failed and skipped entries are already full and are unchanged. `details.partial`, `applied_count`, `failed_count`, and `skipped_count` are unchanged, so `report-builder.ts` partial rendering is unaffected.
- **`progress`** (model-visible, on `browser_fill_form` and `browser_fill_element` successes; also in `details.progress` on an all-failed batch):
  - `filled` (int): eligible census units (a radio group or checkbox set counts once) with a `fill_committed` on the current document epoch.
  - `eligible` (int): census units with `exemption === null`.
  - `remaining` (int): `eligible − filled`.
  - `next` (`{ ref: string; label: string }[]`, at most 10): the first remaining units in document order. A group is listed once, by its first member's ref and the group label. Labels are the census label, sanitized like observation names, at most 60 characters.
  - `complete?: false`: present when the census was bounded (`complete: false`). The counts are then lower bounds.
  - `progress` is omitted when no census is available (browser not launched, or the last observation's epoch differs from the current one) or `eligible === 0`.

  Example:

  ```json
  "progress": { "filled": 20, "eligible": 48, "remaining": 28, "next": [{ "ref": "e31", "label": "Company" }, { "ref": "e32", "label": "Job title" }] }
  ```

### Core: census reuse (`browser/agent-controller.ts`)

- **`latestFillCensus(): FillCensus | null`**: FEAT-055 TASK-001's census, built from the records of the most recent `observe()` with no page read. It returns null when no observation has been taken on the current top-level document epoch. `fillCensus()` (which takes its own read) is unchanged.

### Agent: coverage (`runtime/fulfillment.ts`, owned by FEAT-054)

- **`fillCoverage(census: FillCensus, ledger: readonly ActionLedgerEntry[]): FillCoverage`** (pure): `{ eligible; filled; remaining: readonly { ref; label; groupKey }[]; complete }`. It joins `fill_committed` to census units on the same epoch by ref or `groupKey`. FEAT-054's `evaluateFill` for `all_eligible` must call it, and the progress projection calls it. If FEAT-054 inlined that logic, TASK-005 extracts it with no behavior change, and FEAT-054's coverage tests must stay green unchanged.

### Relationships

- One fill call → 1 final `observe()` (existing) → 1 `latestFillCensus()` (no read) → 1 `fillCoverage()` with the run's action ledger → 0..1 `progress`.
- One text fill → `enter-text` → (`reaction-check` | skipped) → (`watch-and-select` | skipped). Exactly one of `reaction-check` and the declared entry gates `watch-and-select`.
- `FILL_FORM_MAX_FIELDS` 1:1 schema `maxItems` 1:1 `batch-limit` `limit`.

### Indexes & Constraints

- A plain-input text fill issues at most `ceil(REACTION_PROBE_MS / REACTION_POLL_MS) + 1` reaction reads and zero reads inside `watchAndSelectOffered`.
- A fill tool call takes exactly as many `observe()` calls as today. Progress adds none (asserted by `vi.spyOn(controller, 'observe')`).
- A model-visible `progress` serializes to ≤ 1 KiB.

FEAT-056 changes the committed read, and this feature changes when the watch runs. `observeReaction` must use the same committed read as the `no-suggestions` branch, so the FEAT-056 fix covers both paths.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. Fill tools keep the `authenticated` sanitization profile. Stored-secret fills (`secret_ref`) keep their single blind rung: they never enter the text plan, so `reaction-check` never runs on them.
- **Error Handling**:
  - Over-cap input is a typed `INVALID_INPUT / batch-limit` with a cause-specific message naming an engineered next move.
  - A missing census or ledger never fails a fill. `progress` is omitted.
  - `observeReaction` returns at the budget deadline like every other read, and never throws on an empty page.
- **Logging**:
  - The full recovery ledger for every applied field is recorded in `tool-calls.jsonl` under `details.applied`, and masked with `maskUserInputDeep` like all details.
  - The model receives compact summaries, and detail only for failed or escalated fields (plan §11).
  - `progress` labels are page text: sanitized before they become model-visible, and never logged to Pino.
  - No value is added to any log.
- **Security**:
  - A protected control's value never enters `progress`, compact entries, or the reaction probe's result. Compaction keeps FEAT-056's `withheld` verdict and never re-adds `committed` for a withheld control.
  - The fill engine still never presses Enter. A test asserts that no `press('Enter')` occurs on any TASK-002 path.
- **Generality** (memory: never write website-specific logic): every signal (`role`, `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-haspopup`, `list`, observed popup) is structural. Fixtures are synthetic and carry no site names.
- **Compatibility**:
  - No persisted schema changes.
  - Older `tool-calls.jsonl` files lack `details.applied`, and readers must treat it as optional.
  - Saved workflows are untouched. Replay benefits from TASK-002 through the shared engine.
- **TODO entries** (appended to `.spec-lite/TODO.md` at breakdown time):
  - engine-partitioned large fill batches (deviation 1);
  - undeclared popups later than `REACTION_PROBE_MS` (deviation 5);
  - native `<datalist>` option selection (deviation 2).

### Implementation clarifications (2026-10-17)

- The calibrated probe is **325 ms**, with reads at 0/150/300 ms. The initial 450 ms window missed the sixty-second controlled-fixture target; the 300 ms undeclared popup still commits in both the protocol and real-Chrome cases. The baseline records 27 full-watch reaction reads per ordinary field and 9,272 model-applied bytes for ten original plain fills.
- The source still re-observed even an already registered eNN ref, contrary to the assumption in this spec. Ref resolution now reuses the current-document registry, with the controller's epoch and identity healing retained. Name resolution still observes; progress adds no page read. The constant lives in dependency-free `fill-limits.ts` and is re-exported from `browser-fill-form.ts` to avoid a profiles/tool runtime cycle.
- The fixture has **40 physical controls and 38 eligible units**: its three radios form one unit. Continuation fills four bounded batches, followed by one correction call. Tests count semantic sends separately from engine-owned mutations: the refused number control can use its existing typing recovery internally, while no committed field is resent or re-driven. Ordinary ten-field batches have the fifteen-second gate; the batch containing the intentional refusal also pays for recovery.
- The number control rejects invalid native validity states through its input listener; HTML max/step alone mark invalidity but do not prevent a value from being stored. Short, valid synthetic values isolate interaction cost; historical baseline timings are informational and used longer synthetic email/URL/text values. Operation-count and compact-byte comparisons are pinned independently of that timing difference.
- `agent-v12` is added to the manifest's accepted prompt versions and generated protocol artifacts; older versions remain valid.
